_about: Owner rulings of 5 Oct 2026 (GRADER-CORE-1 spec WHY, rulings (2)-(7)) applied to the examiner-verified expectations (data/verify/items.verified.json + data/supplement/items.supplement.json). The loader (lib/data.cjs applyRepins) applies each row ONLY if the current value still equals `old`, and throws otherwise, so a later edit to the verified set cannot be silently overwritten. Rows with `kind: settled` change no value: the ruling settles a contest the audit left open in favour of the verified value, so `contested` becomes false. Rows with `kind: added` add a field the verified set did not carry (v2-only fields are scored only on responses produced with acceptsV2). Cases the rulings do not settle keep their verified value and are listed under `unsettled`.

rulings.2: A miscopied value is penalised ONCE (silly); the work after it earns ECF marks.
rulings.3: A wrongly formed equation then solved correctly loses the forming marks and earns the solving marks (ECF). 'Departure = zero' is kept ONLY for answering a different problem or using an invalid method.
rulings.4: Crossed-out / withdrawn work is not assessed.
rulings.5: No deduction for missing state symbols.
rulings.6: Maths units follow the question's scheme; a silent scheme means no deduction. Science keeps unit deductions.
rulings.7: Mistake type: copied wrongly = silly, performed wrongly = calculation, method misunderstood = conceptual, CBSE format only = presentation, unattempted = no type.
rulings.A17-1: A17 owner ruling (GRADING-JOBS-1, 2026-10-06): a missing or wrong unit on the FINAL answer of a quantity-valued answer costs exactly ½ in Maths AND Science, at most ½ per question, typed presentation; never on a pure number. SUPERSEDES ruling 6's Maths half.
rulings.A17-3: A17 owner ruling 3 AS CHANGED BY THE OWNER 2026-10-06 (supersedes the spec text "Hinglish never deducted"): CBSE answers are in English or in Hindi in Devanagari; an answer written in Hinglish (Roman-script Hindi mixed with English) keeps its content marks and loses exactly 1/2 once per answer, typed presentation (exam technique), comment "Write in English (or Hindi in Devanagari): board examiners expect one medium." English with technical terms and Devanagari Hindi are never penalised; no other language deduction.
rulings.MCQ-TYPE-2: Owner ruling 2026-10-23 (~20:45 IST), MCQ-TYPE-2: a RIGHT MCQ with flawed uploaded working shows the mistake category and is saved to MI as a mistake with 0 marks lost (a habit to fix, never lost marks); the mark stays full. SUPERSEDES, for objective questions with working only, the earlier position 'no type on full marks' (audit GA-15).
rulings.BAL-1: Owner ruling 5 Nov 2026 (GRADER-BALANCE-1): grade a little stricter than a CBSE examiner. An equation with the right species that is not balanced loses exactly 1/2, once per equation, never more for balancing alone. Type by what the student wrote: wrong species or a formula/subscript changed to force a balance = conceptual; coefficients written but wrong = calculation; correct species left skeletal = presentation by default, conceptual only with on-paper evidence of a failed balancing attempt elsewhere. SUPERSEDES S4a ('unbalanced when asked = conceptual') and the D33 settlement of GS-S12-a.

Right option (D), flawed working: the student writes αβ = k instead of αβ = c/a = k/3 and then picks the option by approximating 4/3 — the zeroes-coefficients relation is misapplied, a method not understood (ruling 7: conceptual), exactly the comment the verified case already allows ('αβ should be k/3 (c/a), not k'). The mark stays 1/1; the type is a 0-mark habit (MCQ-TYPE-2).

Right option (C), flawed justification: the student rejects R because 'the total surface area of a sphere is 2πr²' — the TSA of a sphere is 4πr², so the reason rests on a wrong formula, a principle not understood (ruling 7: conceptual), exactly the comment the verified case already allows ('TSA of a sphere is 4πr², not 2πr²'). Not presentation (it changes whether the reasoning is right), not calculation (no operation performed wrongly), not silly (nothing copied from the student's own line). The mark stays 1/1; the type is a 0-mark habit (MCQ-TYPE-2).

Right option (C), flawed working: the student writes the F1 genotype as Rryy (it is RrYy) and says round and yellow appear 'because round and yellow are recessive traits' — they are DOMINANT. Dominance, the principle the answer rests on, is not understood (ruling 7: conceptual), exactly the comment the verified case already allows ('round and yellow are DOMINANT, not recessive'). The mark stays 1/1; the type is a 0-mark habit (MCQ-TYPE-2).
